finding.claim: The purge handler calls checkPerm(u, "admin") but discards the boolean result, so the admin check is never enforced. Any caller who reaches the handler can run purgeAll(). Unlike rotateKeys, it never returns a 403.
finding.source: Any request that reaches the purge handler, including a low-privilege authenticated user whose User.Perms lacks "admin".
finding.sink: purgeAll() at handlers.go:27, a destructive purge-everything operation.

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) loads the user from the request context
checkPerm(u, "admin") returns a bool that is ignored, so there is no early return or error response
The handler responds "purged" to the caller

finding.guards_checked: checkPerm only returns a value and writes no response. No middleware or router is present in the directory, so no outer authorization guard was found. The sibling handler rotateKeys correctly uses mustPerm and returns on failure (handlers.go:33-35), which shows the intended pattern. A middleware outside this directory was not checked.

verdict.guard_found: none (checkPerm at handlers.go:12-14 only returns a bool, and its result is discarded at handlers.go:26; no middleware or router exists in the directory)
verdict.reason: handlers.go:26 calls checkPerm(u, "admin") as a bare statement, so its bool result (handlers.go:12-14) is discarded and purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any caller, unlike rotateKeys, which returns on mustPerm failure (handlers.go:33-35). The only residual uncertainty is an outer middleware outside this directory, which could not be checked.
